title: NNSA transition rows preserve agency and independent authority boundaries
publisher: U.S. Department of Energy and National Nuclear Security Administration
summary: Transitions into GAO source versions are classified as authority changes requiring review rather than substitutions for NNSA object state. Denominator: Fifty-four object transitions with explicit from- and to-authority fields.
key_findings: Finding: Transitions into GAO source versions are classified as authority changes requiring review rather than substitutions for NNSA object state.
Denominator: Fifty-four object transitions with explicit from- and to-authority fields.
Boundary: GAO assessment does not become an agency assertion.
Boundary: Agency budget language does not establish independent closure.
Boundary: Authority change is not outcome change.
Next action: Keep every independent assessment and recommendation status as a separate evidence layer.
why_it_matters: The record turns complete Phase 57J decisions into explicit longitudinal controls without manufacturing an operating transition.
ftfn_relevance: Adds denominator-aware longitudinal structure to the Phase 57J rails.
Makes transition and reopening decisions machine-readable and auditable.
Separates classified change, missing evidence, operating outcomes, implementation, capability, acceptance, and closure.
evidence_limits: Not publicly acquired does not mean nonexistent, withheld, or never submitted.
FTFN public-source research is not agency contact or a submitted FOIA request.
GAO assessment does not become an agency assertion.
Agency budget language does not establish independent closure.
Authority change is not outcome change.
The inherited 1 Closed / 21 Partially Closed / 2 Open entity ledger remains unchanged.
